description: Frontend correctness pass: make profile/settings updates actually persist to the backend, fix the onboarding flow (persist to user.onboarding, fix fullname mapping, guard against null user, resolve 'step 4 empty'), reconcile all frontend service calls against real backend routes (removing/repointing calls to nonexistent /auth/* endpoints), wire the already-built Teams/Projects UI to existing backend routes, and add the simple 'add user' + 'view previous onboards' management UI using existing endpoints. Keep it simple; do not add new complex features. Depends on FEAT-002 (backend auth now honors the session, so authenticated calls succeed).
steps: PROFILE PERSISTENCE: In frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx add an async action `updateProfile(profileData)` that calls userService.updateProfile(profileData), and on success dispatches UPDATE_USER with the returned server user (response.data.user) and returns it. Keep the existing local-only `updateUser` for optimistic local state, but ensure Settings/Profile save flows call the persisting `updateProfile`. Wire frontend/src/pages/Settings.jsx and frontend/src/pages/Profile.jsx (and frontend/src/components/settings/AdvancedSettings.jsx, frontend/src/components/profile/UserProfile.jsx as applicable) to call the persisting path and surface success/error via the existing toast/notification pattern.

ENDPOINT RECONCILIATION (authService): In frontend/src/services/authService.js, repoint updateUserProfile from PUT /auth/profile to PUT /users/profile (reuse userService.updateProfile shape). Replace getUserTeams/getUserProjects usage so they call existing GET /teams and GET /projects (via teamService/projectService) OR remove them if unused after the AuthContext change. Repoint or remove validateTeamInvite (backend has GET /teams/invite/:inviteCode/info), joinTeamByInvite (POST /teams/join/:inviteCode), leaveTeam/leaveProject (use DELETE /teams/:id/members/:userId etc. or remove if unused). The end state: no runtime call targets a nonexistent backend route. Grep the services dir for '/auth/' and confirm only /auth/register,/auth/login,/auth/logout,/auth/me remain.

AUTHCONTEXT refreshUserTeamsAndProjects: update it to use existing endpoints (GET /teams, GET /projects) or make it resilient (try/catch, no throw) so a failure never breaks auth/session bootstrap. Ensure it never calls /auth/teams or /auth/projects.

ONBOARDING FIXES (frontend/src/components/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.jsx): (a) Fix ProfileStep field mapping: use user?.fullname (not fullName) and submit { fullname, jobTitle, company, timezone } to the persisting updateProfile. (b) Persist onboarding progress: on each step advance and on complete, call updateProfile with { onboarding: { currentStep, completedSteps: [...], completed } } so user.onboarding is saved server-side (backend updateProfile already supports this). (c) Drive the 'already completed' gate from user?.onboarding?.completed (fall back to the localStorage flag) so completed users are not re-shown the flow and in-progress users resume at their saved currentStep. (d) Guard every step component and renderStepContent against a null/undefined user so 'Step 4' (FirstTaskStep, index 3) and all steps render safely even before user data loads (this resolves the reported empty step which stems from the prior 401 auth cascade leaving user null). (e) Keep the modal UX; do not redesign it.

ADD USER + VIEW PREVIOUS ONBOARDS: Using existing endpoints only, add a simple management UI. On frontend/src/pages/Users.jsx (or a small dedicated section/page reachable from it): (1) 'Add User' action that opens a simple form and calls POST /api/auth/register with { fullname, username, email, password } (existing endpoint) then refreshes the user list. (2) 'Previous onboards' view: fetch users via userService.getAllUsers (GET /api/users, which returns each user's onboarding object) and render a table/list showing fullname, email, onboarding.completed (yes/no), onboarding.currentStep, and onboarding.completedAt. Keep styling consistent with existing Tailwind components. No new backend routes.

AVATAR UPLOAD (frontend): confirm userService.uploadAvatarFile posts multipart to /upload/avatar and reads response.data.avatar / response.data.publicId (it does). Ensure the calling component (profile/settings avatar upload) invokes it and updates the user via the persisting updateProfile or by using the returned avatar URL. Handle the 503 CLOUDINARY_NOT_CONFIGURED case with a friendly message.

TARGETED FRONTEND TESTS: Add/adjust tests only for what you changed. In frontend/src/services/__tests__ and frontend/src/context/__tests__: test that AuthContext.updateProfile calls userService.updateProfile and updates state from the server response; test authService no longer references removed /auth/* endpoints (or that repointed methods hit the expected URLs, using a mocked apiService). Do NOT try to fix unrelated pre-existing failing component tests.

Run `cd frontend && npm run build` and ensure it succeeds. Run the targeted tests you added/changed and ensure they pass. Record the overall frontend test summary in findings (unrelated pre-existing failures are acceptable and should be listed as known-issues, not fixed here).
acceptance_criteria: Saving profile/settings sends PUT /users/profile and the updated fields persist (state reflects the server response); no code path issues a local-only update that silently drops data.
grep for "/auth/" in frontend/src/services shows only register, login, logout, and me; no runtime frontend call targets a nonexistent backend route.

Onboarding uses user.fullname, persists progress into user.onboarding via the backend, resumes/【skips based on user.onboarding.completed, and renders all steps (including step 4 / FirstTaskStep) without crashing when user is momentarily null.

Users page provides an 'Add User' action (POST /api/auth/register) and a 'previous onboards' listing (from GET /api/users) showing onboarding completed/currentStep/completedAt, using existing endpoints only.
frontend `npm run build` succeeds; added/changed targeted tests pass.
verification: export PATH=/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin:$PATH && cd frontend && npm run build 2>&1 | tail -6
export PATH=/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin:$PATH && grep -rn "/auth/" frontend/src/services | grep -vE "/auth/(register|login|logout|me)" || echo NO_STALE_AUTH_ENDPOINTS
findings:
WHAT CHANGED:
- AuthContext.jsx: added async updateProfile(profileData) that calls userService.updateProfile, dispatches UPDATE_USER with the SERVER user (response.data.user), syncs localStorage, and returns the updated user (throws on failure). Kept local-only updateUser. Fixed refreshUserTeamsAndProjects to call teamService.getTeams()/projectService.getProjects() (real GET /teams, GET /projects) instead of the nonexistent authService.getUserTeams/getUserProjects; those services never throw, so auth bootstrap can't break. Exposed updateProfile in context value.
- authService.js: repointed updateUserProfile from PUT /auth/profile to PUT /users/profile. Removed the 8 methods that targeted nonexistent routes (getUserTeams, getUserProjects, getTeamPermissions, getProjectPermissions, validateTeamInvite, joinTeamByInvite, leaveTeam, leaveProject). End state: only /auth/register,/login,/logout,/me remain as runtime auth calls.
- teamService.js: fixed leaveTeam() which called GET /auth/me but read the wrong response shape; now extracts user id from response.data.data.user (session shape) with a guard. /auth/me is an allowed endpoint.
- Settings.jsx: handleSaveProfile now calls updateProfile (persisting) and surfaces success/error via showSuccess/showError; removed unused userService import.
- Profile.jsx: profile edit, preset avatar change, and Cloudinary file-upload flows now use context updateProfile (was calling no-arg updateUser() which did nothing). Added friendly handling of 503 CLOUDINARY_NOT_CONFIGURED for avatar upload.
- OnboardingFlow.jsx: ProfileStep now uses user?.fullname (was user?.fullName) and submits {fullname,jobTitle,company,timezone} via persisting updateProfile (with saving/error UI). Main flow persists onboarding progress {currentStep,completedSteps,completed} to the backend on each advance and on complete/skip (best-effort, no-throw). 'Already completed' gate driven by user?.onboarding?.completed with localStorage fallback; resumes at saved currentStep. renderStepContent guards against missing step data; all step components are null-user safe via optional chaining, resolving the 'step 4 (FirstTaskStep) empty' symptom that stemmed from the prior 401 cascade leaving user null.
- Users.jsx: fixed broken userService.getUsers call (now getAllUsers). Added an 'Add User' form (POST /api/auth/register with {fullname,username,email,password} then list refresh) and a 'Previous Onboards' table from userService.getAllUsers (GET /api/users) showing fullname, email, onboarding.completed (Yes/No badge), onboarding.currentStep, onboarding.completedAt. Existing endpoints only, existing Bootstrap/Tailwind styling.

TESTS ADDED:
- src/services/__tests__/authService.endpoints.test.js (3 tests): removed helpers are undefined; register/login/logout/me hit correct routes; updateUserProfile targets PUT /users/profile not /auth/profile.
- src/context/__tests__/AuthContext.updateProfile.test.jsx (2 tests): updateProfile calls userService.updateProfile and updates state from the server response (not the local payload) and syncs localStorage; throws on backend failure.
Both files use vitest's vi.* (the repo's pre-existing service tests use jest.* which is not aliased, hence they fail as part of the known baseline).

BUILD: `cd frontend && npm run build` succeeds (vite built in ~4s).

FRONTEND TEST SUMMARY: `npx vitest run` => 233 failed / 161 passed (394 total). Baseline before FEAT-003 was 233 failed / 156 passed; the +5 passing are exactly the new targeted tests, and failures are unchanged (no regressions). KNOWN-ISSUES (pre-existing, NOT in scope, not fixed): ~233 unrelated component/service tests fail largely because they call jest.* which isn't aliased under vitest, plus assorted RTL query mismatches (e.g. ui/__tests__/Input.test.jsx). These are unrelated to FEAT-003.

NOTE: eslint could not run in this env (frontend eslint.config.js imports '@eslint/js' which isn't installed under frontend/node_modules); this is a pre-existing environment gap, and lint is not part of FEAT-003's required verification. The vite build validates imports/syntax for all changed files.

=== REVIEW FIX (2026-08-30 review, Issue 1 - BLOCKING) ===
ISSUE: 'Add User hijacks admin session'. Users.jsx handleAddUser called authService.register, which (a) client-side wrote the created user into localStorage.user, and (b) server-side the register controller called req.logIn(newUser), replacing the admin's Passport session. Net effect: an admin who added a user was silently re-authenticated as that new user.
FIX (option b, simplest correct): added a guarded admin-create branch to backend/controllers/authController.js register: when req.isAuthenticated() is true (an authenticated admin is calling), the controller returns the created user with status 201 WITHOUT calling req.logIn, leaving the caller's session untouched. Public self-registration (unauthenticated) still auto-logs-in as before. On the frontend, added authService.adminCreateUser(userData) which POSTs to /auth/register but does NOT write localStorage; Users.jsx now calls adminCreateUser instead of register. Result: the admin stays logged in as themselves and the new user appears in the Previous Onboards list on refresh.
TESTS: backend tests/routes/auth.test.js gained 'does NOT change the caller session when an authenticated admin creates a user' (session agent creates a second user, asserts GET /api/auth/me still returns the admin) - revert-sensitive. Frontend authService.endpoints.test.js gained 'adminCreateUser posts to /auth/register without overwriting localStorage.user'. The existing 'registers a new user and auto-logs-in' test (unauthenticated) stays green, proving public registration behavior is preserved. Backend npm test green (76 passed/0 failed); frontend build green; targeted vitest suites green.
